title: Louis Vuitton Returns to a Looted Workshop at Asnières, 1871
conflicts: Sources differ on the extent and cause of the damage: Vogue says the workshop was 'looted and destroyed', Numéro 'pillaged' with orders suspended, Biography.com a village in ruins with tools stolen and staff dispersed; a FashionNetwork report (blocked, not cited) says Prussians burned the main atelier, and a dealer blog (offline) blamed the Commune. The story says 'looted', attributes 'destroyed' to Biography.com and names no perpetrator. Striped canvas: 1872 (red and beige, Vogue and Biography.com) versus 1876 (beige and brown, Wikipedia citing Martin); story uses 1872 for the red stripe only.
notes: No first-hand account by Louis Vuitton survives in the sources found; all are later secondary histories, and the story says so ('None of these accounts records what he said or thought'). Louis Vuitton's own heritage pages, Britannica and Quartz are blocked for the verifier and Internet Archive did not load from here, so the edition rests on Biography.com, Numéro, British Vogue, an ESCP archive note and Montecristo Magazine.
